title: Philip II of Macedon wins at Chaeronea
summary: Philip II of Macedon and his son Alexander defeated an alliance led by Athens and Thebes at Chaeronea in Boeotia.
reason: Macedon was expanding south, and Athens, urged on by Demosthenes, joined Thebes to stop Philip.
significance: The victory ended the independence of the Greek city states and gave Macedon control of Greece.
